clue.text: Dropout from Tennessee, one getting imprisoned by magistrate

indicators.note: being imprisoned by something means being held inside it, so the magistrate's word wraps round the others

parts.note: BEAK is British slang for a magistrate
TN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Tennessee
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A student who quit Tennessee ends up jailed by a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1950s Beat Generation figure was the classic dropout from conventional society, so the word fits a social rebel.

clue.text: Lifted bats to cosh

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is raised up, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: bats is informal for crazy, as is nuts

explanation.surface: Someone raises their bats to club a victim.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh is to hit someone over the head, leaving them dazed or senseless; a synonym.

clue.text: Alloy of gold with molybdenum and lutetium

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
Mo is the chemical symbol for molybdenum
Lu is the chemical symbol for lutetium

explanation.surface: A chemist describes an alloy made from gold, molybdenum and lutetium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is a gilded copper-zinc alloy used to decorate furniture and clocks, an example of an alloy.

clue.text: Wooden panel Jock attached to wagon

indicators.note: attached to says the Scot piece is fixed onto the end of the wagon piece

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon
Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A Scotsman fixes a wooden board to his cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscoting is wooden panelling on the lower part of interior walls; one board is a wooden panel.

clue.text: Female bird of the heron family apparently shows bad feeling

parts.note: the bittern is a wading bird related to the heron
-ess is a suffix making a female form, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A female heron-like bird seems to be in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' flags that a female bittern would, by the -ess pattern, be called this, though no such word exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness is resentment or rancour, a synonym for bad feeling.

clue.text: Send into ecstasy Eastern recluse

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy
to remit is to send, as with payment

explanation.surface: Something sends an Eastern hermit into rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send into ecstasy' reads as one phrase meaning delight; split it: REMIT goes into position after E, then another E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious hermit living apart, a synonym for recluse.

clue.text: Partners back type of film

parts.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table, giving W and E
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Two partners finance a certain kind of movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A Western is a film genre set in the American Old West, so an example of a kind of movie.

clue.text: Avarice could provide a luxury

indicators.note: the letters of the word avarice could, rearranged, provide something else

explanation.surface: Greed may lead to some indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare, sturgeon roe, is the archetypal expensive delicacy and an example of a luxury.

clue.text: Sneaked craftily with mask on in children's game

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed on top of, so the mask piece comes first

parts.note: to mask something is to hide it

indicators.note: craftily suggests sneaked's letters are cunningly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks about wearing a mask during a kids' game.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide-and-seek is a classic playground pastime where one player searches for the others.

clue.text: Varying tones I rant in a loud voice

indicators.note: varying the arrangement of tones, I and rant gives a new word

explanation.surface: Someone shouts, changing pitch as they rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was a Greek herald with a powerful voice; stentorian describes speech that is very loud and booming.

clue.text: Tense English politician — one won't be in office long

definitions.text: one won't be in office long

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A nervous English MP will not keep the seat for long.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary office worker, someone employed only briefly.

clue.text: Medicine can make better swallowing first of tablets

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: swallowing means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: to cure is to make better

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of tablets

explanation.surface: A canned remedy heals once you swallow the pills.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is a medicinal extract dissolved in alcohol, a kind of remedy.

clue.text: Drink tea with old actor around America

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: around tells us the actor's name goes round the abbreviation for America

parts.note: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: An old thespian drinks tea while touring the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Rear Admiral taken in by clever clergyman

indicators.note: taken in by says the admiral's letters are held inside the clever word

parts.note: cute can mean shrewd or clever
RA is the naval abbreviation for Rear Admiral

explanation.surface: A senior naval officer is fooled by a cunning priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant priest in the Church of England, a type of clergyman.

clue.text: Essex town providing staff for large plant

parts.note: manning a post means providing staff for it
a tree is a large plant

explanation.surface: An Essex town supplies workers for a large factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but here it is a living plant. Essex is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Manningtree is a small market town in Essex, on the River Stour, so an example of a town there.

clue.text: Whence came invaders and not familiar politician

parts.note: nor means and not
Mandy was the familiar nickname of Labour politician Peter Mandelson

explanation.surface: Invaders arrived, but not a well-known politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans who conquered England in 1066 came from this region of northern France.

clue.text: Finished holding mark of injury in scrap

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: did, as in did the job, means finished it
a scar is the mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: A fighter ends up scarred after a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight, but here it is a verb: throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to get rid of it, a synonym for scrap as a verb.

clue.text: Person striking out individual trapped by mole

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: a mole is a harbour breakwater, like a pier
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A lone figure is caught by a burrowing animal while going on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer strikes out into new territory, someone forging ahead first.

clue.text: Great chance for model

definitions.meaning: in sport, an easy scoring opportunity that should not be missed
someone who poses for an artist or photographer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an easy opportunity in sport and a person who poses for a portrait.

clue.text: Material for coats makes waterproof sort mostly

parts.note: to seal is to make watertight

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: kind means sort or type

explanation.surface: A waterproofing treatment is mostly applied to coat fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelt of a seal was used for fur coats, a material for outerwear.

clue.text: A cricketer on tour

parts.note: Stuart Broad is an England fast bowler

explanation.surface: A cricketer is away on a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being overseas, as a touring team is.

clue.text: Nuclear expert comes out in spots

indicators.note: comes out here means the expert stands outside, round the other letter

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A nuclear scientist breaks out in a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, so the spots on a teenager's face.

clue.text: One electrical safety precaution gives a narrow escape

definitions.meaning: connecting an appliance to ground is one protection against shock
a close shave, something only just avoided

explanation.definitionFit: Split one way it is a single grounding connection; split another it is a close call.

clue.text: Mess with drug

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a jumbled mess and the cannabis product hashish.

clue.text: Salvation Army in unfinished campaign

indicators.note: in places the army's initials inside the other word

parts.note: crude means rough or unfinished

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army mounts a rough-and-ready campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous campaign for a cause, originally a medieval holy war.

clue.text: Supernatural creature has been disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of has been are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A ghostly being has been stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a female spirit whose wail foretells death.
